claims.text: In Pulumi, calling toString on an Output<T> produces placeholder text of the form `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` instead of the resolved value (e.g., in a log line, generated file, or resource property).
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi produces the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when an update conflicts with another in-progress update, and the update-conflicts page addresses it.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
The Pulumi CLI emits a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend.
The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml.
On Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi dev builds provide pre-release builds giving access to bug fixes that haven't shipped in a stable release yet.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an 'automatic-logging' section.
`pulumi destroy` can fail, and the destroy-failures page handles those scenarios.
Pulumi Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com provides community support.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Outputs are central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The Pulumi docs have pages at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ covering accessing single outputs with Apply and working with multiple outputs.

When an output value is concatenated, logged or converted to a string directly instead of via `apply`, Pulumi does not raise an error by default but silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In Pulumi TypeScript, string conversion of an Output yields literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, string conversion of an Output yields literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Pulumi Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the function to use to serialize outputs to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Pulumi Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In Pulumi C#, string conversion of an Output yields literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes Pulumi throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text when an output is converted to a string, supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#.
`pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are the string-composition helpers for outputs in TypeScript.
`Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are the string-composition helpers for outputs in Python.
`pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are the string-composition helpers for outputs in Go.
`Output.Format` is the string-composition helper for outputs in C#.
The value read from an output inside an apply callback is only available inside that callback or in outputs derived from it.

The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished running, so an outer variable assigned within it is `undefined` when read earlier.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix the issue.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, while a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi output is generally always true because the output object itself is evaluated rather than its eventual value.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
In the example, `vpc.vpcId.apply((id) => ...)` derives a new Output whose value depends on the branch; `aws.ec2.Vpc` exposes a `vpcId` output property.
Passing an output as a resource's logical name or loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

Dependent resources whose names or counts depend on values only known after provisioning can be restructured into a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a StackReference.

Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output; awaiting an output or reading it synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A StackReference lets one Pulumi program consume another stack's outputs as inputs.
The Automation API's result of running an update has an `outputs` field (`res.Outputs` in Go).
